effort: Keep the pelvis supported over the foot during small frontal and diagonal force demands.
brief: This consolidation exposure addresses unwanted side-to-side pelvic motion in stance, not sport cutting. E1 supplies a small lateral rhythm marker; E2/E3 use limited single-leg acceptance in diagonal and lateral vectors. Raised two-foot receiving, split-stance forward release and a grounded lateral step-up express force with different support conditions. Light arch and trunk work set up targeted hip/adductor strength.
marker: Count centred contacts in each six-hop lateral set while pelvis and feet face forward, without crossing feet or increasing travel. Keep the same small gap. Lateral-hop rhythm cannot be compared numerically with fore-aft or stationary pogo performance.
review: Class 5 prescribed twelve bilateral landings and eight primary rounds emphasizing hips/hamstrings. No actual response is known. Class 6 reintroduces ten single-leg receiving events, matching the written Class 3 count rather than increasing that exposure; primary volume falls to seven rounds while frontal strength roles replace some posterior-chain work.
sequence: The bilateral lateral ankle task comes first, then the short single-leg tasks before fatigue. Raised bilateral receiving and two planted/supporting-force tasks complete the explosive block without a long bound circuit.

E.name: Line Pogo Side-to-Side
E.job: Main frontal foot-return task with a small repeatable displacement.
E.cue: Both feet together, hop sideways across a seam or imaginary line marked by cones outside the area; less than one foot length of travel. Keep toes/pelvis forward and knees soft. Shorten travel for rolling ankles or hip sway.

E.name: Single-Leg Diagonal Hop to Stick
E.job: Accept a small combined forward/lateral push over one leg, controlling the pelvis across two directions.
E.cue: Hop forward and slightly outward on the same leg over no more than one own foot length; hold 2 s. Walk back. Keep the diagonal consistent and modest; reduce distance for knee drift or hip rotation.

E.name: Skater Bound to Stick
E.job: Transfer body mass from one leg to the other through a short lateral push and stable receiving stance.
E.cue: Start on the opposite foot, push a short distance sideways, land on the named leg and hold 2 s. Reset by walking before another attempt to that side. No long-distance reach, crossover sweep or repeated alternating sequence; shorten distance for extra steps.

E.name: Lateral Box Jump — two-foot landing
E.job: Express a frontal push with shared receiving at a low raised surface, reducing dependence on single-leg landing skill.
E.cue: Stand beside a suitably low stable box; small two-foot jump sideways onto it, face forward, hold 2 s and step down. No turn or knee tuck. Reduce height/sideways gap for twisting or cramped landing space.

E.name: Split-Stance Medicine Ball Forward Scoop Toss
E.family: asymmetric hip drive with pelvic control
E.job: Direct hip/leg force forward while the split base resists unwanted pelvic rotation.
E.cue: Small stationary split stance, light ball low, shallow dip and fast forward scoop. Both feet remain planted, pelvis faces forward, no twist or catch. Reduce ball mass/stance offset if the rear foot pivots or the back arches.

E.name: Explosive Lateral Step-Up — no flight
E.job: Accelerate the body over a laterally positioned stance foot while keeping the pelvis level, without another jump landing.
E.cue: Working foot flat on a low box beside the body. Drive up quickly using that leg; foot remains on the box and free knee lifts slightly, then lower over 2 s. No push or jump from the floor foot; lower box height for hip hike.

S.name: Short-Foot Drill — supported single-leg stance
S.job: Light arch strengthening under one-leg support to maintain a stable contact platform during frontal drift.
S.cue: Use hand support, soft knee and long toes; hold the target arch gently without clawing. Release fully between holds. Use two feet supported instead at the same target-foot holds if single-leg loading causes gripping or cramping.

S.name: Side Plank — knees bent
S.job: Light lateral-trunk strengthening to resist pelvic drop while the lower limb changes support.
S.cue: Forearm under shoulder, knees bent, lift into a shoulder–hip–knee line and breathe easily. Keep the upper hip stacked; shorten hold or lower hips slightly for shaking. This remains easy before the challenging adductor task.

P.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides
P.cue: Floor split stance, front foot planted, pelvis square; lower 2 s and rise firmly for 1 s. Reduce load/range for collapse or balance loss. Use one DB with stable hand support instead of two unsupported DBs if needed; counts stay the same.
P.job: Retain the main stance-leg knee/hip force anchor with a stable base.

P.name: Goblet Lateral Lunge
P.cue: Hold one DB securely at chest. Step sideways, sit into the stepping hip with full foot planted, return to centre without jumping; 3 s out/down, 1 s return. Keep knee with toes and pelvis square. Shorten step/range or reduce DB for inward knee collapse.
P.job: Add direct frontal hip/knee force for accepting small lateral displacement.
P.decision: New 1 × 6 per side replaces a posterior-chain accessory role for this frontal emphasis. Load only through observed control; do not chase depth or add a second set automatically.

P.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift — hand supported, dumbbell
P.cue: One DB opposite working leg, free hand on stable support. Soft stance knee, free leg travels back, pelvis faces floor; lower 3 s and rise 1 s. Support removes balance as the limiter. Reduce load/range for hip opening or trunk rotation.
P.job: Retain supported single-leg hip force while keeping the pelvis square.
P.decision: Return to Class 3's supported 1 × 6 per leg; that written prescription is a reference, not evidence of performed load or tolerance.

P.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated dumbbells
P.cue: Both legs together, knees near 90°, heels start on floor, hands secure DBs on lower thighs above knees. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load for bounce/lost heel height. If bench fit is unsuitable, use supported standing bent-knee calf raises instead, same reps/rest, and log changed knee angle.
P.job: Maintain a small knee-flexed ankle-force set while frontal control tasks change.

P.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — supported single leg
P.cue: Work from floor, near-straight soft knee, one DB and stable hand support. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load or use bodyweight for lost range; use 1 × 8 bilateral instead of per-leg work if even unilateral bodyweight is too demanding, with 1 × 4 bilateral preparation.
P.job: Return to the established single straight-knee calf set per leg for ankle-force coverage.
P.decision: Class 4's 1 × 8 per leg returns after a hip-focused class omitted it. This is role coverage, not accumulated tolerance.

P.name: Copenhagen Plank — Short Lever
P.cue: Top knee on a suitable stable bench, forearm under shoulder, bottom leg clear; hold a straight shoulder–pelvis–knee line while breathing. Select support so 15 s is challenging with about 5 s clean hold available. If support/lever is unsuitable, use side-lying hip adduction instead: 1 × 8 per side, 2 s up/1 s hold/2 s down, light 1 × 3 preparation, same side/round rests; add a hand-secured DB above the lower knee only if needed for the strength effort.
P.job: Challenge adductor force for pelvic support over the stance leg.
P.decision: New short-lever 15 s per side; choose a manageable support/lever with about five clean seconds available. Use the stated dynamic replacement when bench or lever does not fit.

equipment: Boxes for E4/E6 must be low, stable and wide enough; if E4 is unsuitable, use a two-foot lateral jump to floor stick instead, 1 × 2 per direction, same rest, four two-foot landings. For E6 without a suitable low box, use a fast shallow lateral-lunge return to a stable two-foot stand instead, 1 × 4 per direction at the same rest, no flight. E5 needs contained throwing clearance; use a split-stance held-ball hip drive without release instead, same 1 × 3 per lead side and resets/rest, replacing six throws with six held-ball accelerations. P6 requires an appropriate stable knee support or its side-lying adduction replacement.
count_note: Twelve lateral pogo contacts + four diagonal single-leg hops + six opposite-leg bounds + four lateral box landings = 26 events: 16 two-foot and ten single-leg, 42 foot contacts. E4 includes four grounded step-down descents. E5 adds six throws; E6 eight grounded drives. Primary holds total 30 s across both sides, not 30 reps. P6 dynamic replacement changes that 30 s hold exposure to 16 working adduction reps plus six light preparation reps; record the route instead of combining both.
novelty: Six explosive executions differ from prior defaults through lateral rhythm, a diagonal same-leg vector, opposite-leg transfer, raised lateral receiving, split-stance forward release and grounded lateral elevation. The box/step-up/toss choices are related variants with explicit vector/support jobs. The supported single-leg short-foot task deliberately revisits arch control under a changed support condition; it is not claimed as a new exercise family.
audit: Held unilateral receiving to the earlier written ten-event dose and avoided long/skater-continuous bounds in this consolidation class. Reduced primary rounds to seven while replacing hip-thrust/walkout/hip-flexion emphasis with lateral and adductor roles. P6 remains challenging short-lever strength, while S2 is deliberately easy. Checked that step-downs, held seconds and replacement throws are counted separately.
progression: Do not interpret the middle class as proof of adaptation. Use the same recorded split-squat and supported-hinge conditions only when actual data exists; otherwise calibrate anew. The next class may introduce very short linked contacts only with demonstrated current control; no linked sequence is earned by writing Classes 1–6.
map_note: Frontal-control consolidation; ten single-leg landings and seven primary rounds.
next_job: Very short linked elastic contacts with strict current-readiness conditions and no conditioning goal.
handoff: Review Classes 1–6 and any actual feedback, then finalize Class 7 with explicit readiness/replacement criteria before continuing.

other_explosive.name: Split-Stance Medicine Ball Forward Scoop Toss

explosive_exposure_by_exercise.exercise: Split-Stance Medicine Ball Forward Scoop Toss

final_review: Midpoint review: six distinct frontal/diagonal drill executions have specific stance-support jobs; related box/toss/step variants are disclosed. Ten unilateral receiving events match the earlier prescribed count, with no claim they were completed. Seven primary rounds include a challenging short-lever adductor task and explicit dynamic replacement. Held seconds, box descents and no-flight step-ups are separately accounted.
